subject: PyPI project name crawly
description: A March 2026 PEP 541 request seeks the abandoned PyPI name crawly for an active Python SDK. The old project has one beta release from 2012, dead Bitbucket and documentation links, and very low recent download activity.

evidence.claim: The existing crawly package has a single 2012-10-24 beta release and dead project/documentation links.
The requester says crawly is the import name of their active SDK and reports a name mismatch if they publish under another distribution name.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: Current demand for the exact namespace is established by the transfer request, but value is governed by PyPI reassignment and does not imply direct reuse of the old software.

subject: PyPI project name acts
description: A February 2026 PEP 541 request seeks the acts project name, whose existing Android Comms Test Suite package has one release from January 2020 and no later activity according to the request.

evidence.claim: The existing acts project has only one release dated 2020-01-13 and no activity since according to the request.
The request is for reassignment of the exact PyPI namespace to a replacement project.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: The case supports namespace demand and abandonment evidence but little evidence of a product wedge beyond naming/governance.

subject: PyPI project name mori
description: AMD ROCm maintainers requested the PyPI name mori in June 2026 so their actively developed Modular RDMA Interface project can use the upstream name rather than amd-mori. The request describes an active repository with 130+ stars.

evidence.claim: The requester identifies mori as the name of an actively developed AMD ROCm project and says it is already distributed as amd-mori.
The requester states the exact name is needed to align the PyPI distribution name with the import name and upstream repository.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: This is evidence of real ecosystem naming demand, but the value is in governance and discoverability rather than reusing the abandoned artifact.

subject: PyPI project name openalex
description: The official OpenAlex team requested transfer of the openalex PyPI name in February 2026, with the existing owner explicitly agreeing to transfer it. The team wanted to replace the less discoverable openalex-official name.

evidence.claim: The current owner explicitly agreed to transfer the openalex project name to the official OpenAlex team.
The OpenAlex team said it was already publishing its official CLI under openalex-official and wanted the canonical openalex name for discoverability.

decision.label: RESEARCH
decision.reason: This is a useful positive control: namespace value can be realized cleanly through consensual transfer. It is not an abandonment opportunity and should not be conflated with reclaim cases.

subject: PyPI project name idp-common
description: A July 2026 PEP 541 request reports that the public PyPI idp-common package is effectively empty while an AWS public project has an internal dependency with the same name. The requester reports that a clean installation resolves the public package, creating a dependency-confusion hazard.

evidence.claim: The existing idp-common release is a minimal package with no substantive functionality according to static inspection described in the request.
The requester demonstrates that a public dependency on idp_common can resolve to the PyPI package in a clean environment and identifies the resulting dependency-confusion hazard.

decision.label: RESEARCH
decision.reason: This is a negative/defensive control: residual namespace state creates operational risk rather than a safe reuse opportunity. The useful intervention is monitoring and prevention, not taking over the namespace.
